deck: Table Rock this morning: 911.23 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Don't quit at 10.
play.body: Fall is the opposite of August. The bite can last until lunch.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 911.49 early in the week to 911.23 this morning — about 0.26 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. 4 mornings this week the desk had no new gage (carry-forward). Numbers marked “desk” were read from that day’s scout; “carry” was not. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: The lake is nearly 4 feet below full pool, exposing more shoreline, stumps and hazards in shallow coves, upper arms and near some ramps. Boaters should use extra caution, particularly in the James, Kings and Long Creek arms where navigation can tighten and certain launches require a longer walk.

Surface water has cooled into the mid- to upper 60s with excellent clarity. Bass respond well to topwaters and soft plastics early, then shift to jigs, live bait or drop-shot rigs around long points, gravel flats dropping into 20–40 ft, and offshore structure. Mixed-bag action includes walleye on points in 20–25 ft and crappie or spotted bass from deeper brush and docks. Recent patterns show solid catches are possible when presentations match the clear, cooling conditions.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~5,848 cfs on the last printed reading. Not a live hourly. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: This cold tailwater stays productive year-round thanks to deep releases from Table Rock and steady stocking. Generation remains the primary tactic book: lower or minimal flows early create prime windows for wading, light-line drifting or indicator fishing with micro jigs, midges and scuds, while stronger current (often building later) calls for weighted rigs and precise drifts through seams and behind structure.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics or scented/natural baits. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, mega worms or other soft plastics/scented baits for the water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in many areas. Recent reports highlight good rainbow numbers, strong brown activity (especially upper lake and first mile below dam), and success on marabou jigs (black/sculpin/olive, Indy orange head favorite), zebra midges in red/black, scuds, and night fishing with streamers or small jerkbaits. Water clarity is excellent — clean presentations win. Call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA schedule before you wade or launch.
